description: Every §109 cross-version pair in docs/work/enterprise-master-build-checklist-2026-09-16.md, and for each one either the test CI runs or the reason no test can exist yet. scripts/check-cross-version-matrix.mjs fails when a pair is missing, when a covered pair names a test file that is not there, or when a blocked pair does not name what would unblock it. A pair may never be both.

cli.artifacts: GitHub release assets (agiworkforce-linux-x64.tar.gz and four more). The npm package @agiworkforce/cli is scaffolded but unpublished; the registry 404s, which is why localRuntimeClient.ts keeps CLI_IS_PUBLISHED false.

desktop.artifacts: v-desktop-1.2.0 is the only Tauri release and carries the version the tree builds today (Linux .deb/.rpm/.AppImage only), so there is no N-1 desktop artifact.

vscode.artifacts: never published to the Marketplace or Open VSX

chrome.artifacts: never published to the Chrome Web Store

mobile.artifacts: never shipped to TestFlight, App Store or Play

web.artifacts: the UI and its API deploy as one Vercel artifact; no separately versioned backend exists

pairs.title: New web plus old backend
pairs.reason: apps/web serves the UI and every /api route from one Next.js deployment, so there is no backend artifact that can be pinned a version behind the web build. A job that deployed the previous web commit would be testing the previous web, not an old backend.
pairs.unblockedBy: A founder decision to split and separately version the API, or to re-scope this row onto the client/server contract the other pairs already measure.

pairs.title: Old mobile plus new backend
pairs.reason: No mobile build has ever been released. There is no N-1 mobile artifact to install against the current backend, so any job here would be running the current mobile source twice.
pairs.unblockedBy: Founder action: ship mobile 1.2.0 to TestFlight and Play internal testing, so the next build has a released predecessor to pair with.

pairs.title: Old desktop plus new backend
pairs.reason: v-desktop-1.2.0 is the only Tauri release and it carries the same version apps/desktop builds today, so the released artifact is not a predecessor. The Electron shell has never been released at all.
pairs.unblockedBy: The next desktop release. Once a second release exists, 1.2.0 becomes the N-1 artifact this job downloads.

pairs.title: New CLI plus old VS Code
pairs.surrogate: The VS Code extension has never been published, so there is no N-1 extension binary. What an older extension is on the wire is a client that asks for protocol 7, or asks for nothing, and the current app-server is driven through exactly that handshake and then through the method surface such a client uses.

pairs.title: Old CLI plus new VS Code
pairs.surrogate: The released CLI v-cli-1.0.0 is below MINIMUM_SUPPORTED_RUNTIME_VERSION and speaks a protocol the extension refuses. The suite drives the real LocalRuntimeClient against a runtime that answers as that CLI does and asserts the refusal names the side to update.
pairs.command: pnpm --filter agi-workforce exec vitest run src/__tests__/localRuntimeClient.test.ts src/__tests__/cliProtocolContract.test.ts

pairs.title: New Mobile Remote plus old host
pairs.surrogate: An old Desktop host is, on the wire, a QR carrying the legacy agiw: scheme. The suite parses that payload with the shipping parser and asserts the app refuses it and tells the user to update Desktop rather than pairing without the secret.

pairs.title: Old Remote plus new host
pairs.reason: The reverse direction needs a released mobile build to run against the current host, and no mobile build has ever been released. The host side cannot stand in for it: an old Remote is defined by the parser it shipped with, which only exists inside that artifact.
pairs.unblockedBy: Founder action: the same mobile release that unblocks row 1761.

pairs.title: New Chrome plus old bridge
pairs.reason: The native messaging bridge in apps/extension/native-host has never been released as a versioned artifact; it is installed from source by install.sh and declares no wire version, so there is nothing to pin an older build to.
pairs.unblockedBy: A versioned native-host release, which needs the Chrome Web Store listing decision first, and a declared bridge protocol version to negotiate on.

pairs.title: Old Chrome plus new bridge
pairs.reason: The extension has never been published to the Chrome Web Store, so there is no N-1 extension to load against the current bridge.
pairs.unblockedBy: Founder action: publish the Chrome extension, so the next build has a released predecessor.
